full_judgment:
Md Nazrul Islam Talukder J: This is an application for bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused petitioner in Gulshan Police Station Case No. 10 dated 10-4-2018 corresponding to DUDOK GR Case No. 24 of 2018 under section 4 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2012, now pending in the Court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. The case of the prosecution, in short, is that on 10-4-2018, one Md Shamsul Alam, Deputy Director, Anti-Corruption Commission being informant lodged a First Information Report (FIR) with Gulshan Police Station, Dhaka against the accused-petitioner and others alleging, inter-alia, that one Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti, Shareholder, Director and Former Chairman of Audit Committee of Farmers Bank opened 25 bank accounts in various branches of Farmers Bank Limited in his own name and in the name of his wife, son, daughter and other relatives. On 4-11-2013, an amount of Taka 50 (fifty lac) was transferred by way of pay order to Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti's Saving Account No. 0112-0000-0005-2, Gulshan Branch, Farmers Bank Limited from one Shafkat Motin's Saving Account No. 011821080002461, Prime Bank Limited. On 12-11-2013, an amount of Taka 10,00,000 (ten lac) was also transferred by a pay order to Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti's Saving Account No. 0112-0000-0005-2 from Jamuna Bank Limited, Gulshan Branch. Thereafter, on 9-12-2013, a pay order for an amount of Taka 20,00,000 (twenty lac) was issued from Account No 0111-10000-3098, Bakshigonj Branch, Farmers Bank Limited, belonging to Rimi Enterprise and the said amount of money was later transferred to Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti's Saving Account No. 0112-0000-0005-2. An amount of Taka 6,81,88,000 (six crore eighty one lac eighty eight thousand) was found in Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti's Account No. 0112-0000-0238-7, Bakshigonj Branch, Farmers Bank Limited but Zia Uddin Ahmed, former Manager and Md Delowar Hossain, former Manager did not send any information about any Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to Bangladesh Bank in respect to the aforesaid transactions. On 8-1-2014, an amount of Taka 2,00,000,00 (two crore) was transferred by way of pay order to Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti's Saving Account No. 0112-0000-0005-2 from Saif Power Tech Limited's current account No. 0111-1000-0125-8. Apart from these, an amount of Taka 55,00,000 (fifty five lac) was spotted in the accounts of 3- FDR opened in the name of the present accused-petitioner Rashedul Huq Chishti at Gulshan Branch, Farmers Bank Limited but the said amount was enchased and withdrawn on 26.01 i.e before maturity of 3-FDR. Apart from that, on various occasions, 8 (eight) pay orders amounting to Taka 1,34,85,000 (one crore thirty four lac eighty five thousand) were issued in the name of Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti and his other relatives. As per the pay order register of Gulshan Branch, Farmers Bank Limited, it appears that an amount of Taka 1,80,87,000 (one crore eighty lac eighty seven thousand) was deposited in the name of M/s Rashed Enterprise by 16 (sixteen) pay orders. From 18-11-2013 to 30-1-2018, an amount of Taka 138,82,92,642 (one hundred thirty eight crore eighty two lac ninety two thousand six hundred forty two) was deposited in Current Account Number 0111-1000-0236-3 belonging to Bakshigonj Jute Spinners Mills Limited, Bakshigonj Branch and major portion of the said amount was transferred from Gulshan Branch, Farmers Bank Limited and the whole amount was also withdrawn from Bakshigonj Branch. Mohammad Masudur Rahman Khan, Manager, Bakshigonj Branch as well as Zia Uddin Ahmed, former Manager, Gulshan Branch and Md Delowar Hossain, former Manager did not send any information about any Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to Bangladesh Bank in respect of the aforesaid transactions. On 7-3-2017, an amount of Taka 15,00,000 (fifteen lac) was transferred to Md Sharif Chowdhury from Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti's brother Sajedul Huq Chishti's relative and employee Abdul Wadud's organization namely M/s ADM Dyeing and Finishing's bank account in order to purchase share for Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti. On 25-4-2017, an amount of Taka 5,42,50,000 (five crore forty two lac fifteen thousand) loan was disbursed in the account of TONUJ CORPORATION and after disbursing the same, the said amount was transferred to former Director Morshed Murad Ibrahim for purchasing his shares of the bank but the said shares were purchased in the name of Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti and his other relatives. On 7-3-2017, as per the application of Zia Uddin Ahmed, Manager, Gulshan Branch, an amount of Taka 60,00,000 (sixty lac) was issued in favour of Md Shorif Chowdhury, Director of Famers Bank Limited by vide Pay Order No. 0101-591 for purchasing his shares and the said shares were purchased in the name of Md Mahbubul Huq Chishti and his other relatives. On 19-3-2017, an amount of BDT 2,50,00,000 was transferred from Loan Account No. LD 1705130125 of Apartment Design & Development (Pvt.) Limited of the Farmers Bank Limited, Mirpur Branch to Current Account No. 0111-1001-3419-7 of the same Bank. Thereafter, by vide Cheque Nos. 1376031 and 1376032, an amount of Taka 1,25,00,000 each was sent to the Current Account No. 0111-1000-3183-1 of M/s Elma Trading Corporation. Subsequently, on the same day, two pay orders were issued in favour of Babul Chishti and his family members by vide Pay Order No. 0111004 and Pay order No. 0111-007 of an amount of Taka two crore and fifty lac respectively. Besides, from Current Account No. 0111-1002-0367-5 of M/s Jahan Traders, in total 1 crore 40 lac taka was withdrawn and another pay order of Taka 40 lac was issued in favour of Babul Chishti and his family members. On the same day, two pay orders were issued amounting to Taka 2 crore from Current Account No. 01.11-1000-0760-0 of M/s S2RS Corporation of the same bank in favour of the Director Md Sharif Chowdhury. After preliminary inquiry into the aforesaid suspicious transactions, it is found that Mr Md Mahbubul Haque Chishti (Babul Chishti) misappropriated a total amount of Taka (50,00,000 + 20,00,000 + 6,81,88,000 + 2,00,00,000 + 55,00,000 + 1,34,85,000 + 1,80,84,000 + 1,38,82,92,642.26 + 15,00,000 + 2,85,00,000 + 2,50,00,000 + 40,00,000 + 2,00,00,000) = Taka 1,59,95,49,642 (one hundred fifty nine crore ninety five lac forty nine thousand six hundred and forty two Taka) by means of illegal and suspicious transactions, and thereby committed the offence under section 4 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2012 by shifting, converting and transferring the monies to the different persons at different places and locations. Hence, this FIR. 

 3. It may be noted that the investigation of the case is under way. It is stated in the application that the accused-petitioner was arrested on 10-4-2018 and since that time, he is in jail custody. 

 11. He candidly submits that the accused-petitioner is neither a director nor a chairman of Farmers Bank but he has been implicated in this case simply for the reason that he the son of Mahbubul Haque Chishti, Director and former Chairman of Audit Committee of Farmer is Banks and on this scenario of the case, the accused-petitioner may be enlarged on bail. 

 12. He categorically submits that though the FIR was lodged on 10-4-2018, no charge-sheet has been submitted against the accused-petitioner and others by the investigating officer till today and the accused-petitioner for that reason cannot be detained or remained in custody for an indefinite period and considering this aspect of the case, the accused-petitioner may be enlarged on bail. 

 14. He submits that since no prima-facie case as to money laundering offence against the accused-petitioner has been disclosed, the accused-petitioner should be enlarged on bail. 

 16. He lastly submits that the there is no suspicious transaction against the accused-petitioner in the FIR and considering this aspect of the case, the accused-petitioner may be enlarged on bail. 

 18. He vehemently submits that from a plain reading of the FIR, it is very much noticeable that there are specific and definite allegations of money laundering against the accused-petitioner and others and that the blue print towards commission of the money laundering will come to the light very soon as serious and repulsive activities of the accused-petitioner and others in misappropriating money through illegal suspicious transactions are forthcoming to the investigating officer and to the other authorities and considering this aspect of the case, the accused-petitioner should not be enlarged on bail until the investigating officer submits report in the instant case and for this reason, the accused-petitioner should not be enlarged on bail at this stage. 

 23. On the other hand, in reply to objection raised by Mr Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, the learned Attorney-General submits that the information figured out in his Bengali written arguments was verbally received by him from Bangladesh Bank and other authorities from which it is clear that the evidence as to involvement of the accused-petitioner in the money laundering offence is forthcoming against the accused-petitioner from different sources and the truthfulness of the allegation of money laundering will he clearly disclosed alter investigation of the case, and he being the Chief Law Officer of the country after getting the information has simply formulated the submissions in Bengali in order to have appreciated the same with proper perspective and considering those aspects of the case, the accused-petitioner should not he enlarged on bail at this stage. 

 24. He next submits that the accused-petitioner earlier submitted Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 22653 of 2018 for bail but the same was discharged for non prosecution on 1-8-2018 as prayed for by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner and, as such, the application for bail within a short span of time from the date of discharge is always disapproved by this Court and considering this picture of the case, the accused-petitioner should not be enlarged on bail. 

 25. In reply to this submission, Mr Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, appearing for the accused-petitioner, submits that it is true that the accused-petitioner earlier filed a miscellaneous case for bail but the accused-petitioner has come before this Court against the subsequent rejection order of bail so this matter is not same with that of the earlier matter and there is no bar to filing any application for bail before this Court against any order rejecting application for bail by the learned Special Judge and, as such, there is no bar to coming before this Court for bail in spite of the fact that the Rule for bail was discharged for non-prosecution. 

 27. He next submits that the money laundering offence is also termed as white collar crime which goes through a different complex series of transaction and, as such, it cannot be said that the accused-petitioner is not involved in the money laundering offence until the investigating report is submitted in the instant case. 

 30. He further submits that it is true that FIR named accused No. 6 was enlarged on bail by this case, but the case of the present accused-petitioner case is quite distinguishable than that of the co-accused and, as such, it cannot be said that the present accused-petitioner may be enlarged on bail as he remains in the same footing with that of the co-accused. 

 32. Upon hearing the submissions made by the respective parties, it is worthwhile to mention that the present case brought against the accused-petitioner and others relates to predicate offences which are generally committed by 27 modes and means. The offences of money laundering perpetrated through corruption and bribery are all the schedule offences of the Anti-Corruption Commission. The meaning of the word "corruption" is very wide and it has far reaching effect. The money laundering has been defined and described as predicate offence which is committed resorting to corruption and bribery. The money laundering offence is also termed as white collar crimes. Many white-collar crimes are especially difficult to prosecute because the perpetrators use sophisticated means to conceal their activities through a series of complex transactions. The money laundering is a financial crime which are committed and carried out by individuals, corporations or by organized crime groups for the purpose of generating huge profits. In order to give colour of legitimacy, these profits are laundered by the criminals. Corrupt public officials launder their ill-gotten bribes and kick-backs to give them the colour of legitimacy, if the money laundering offences are unchecked, money-laundering can destabilize the financial system and undermine development efforts in emerging markets. It weakens the social fabric and collective ethical standard. Money laundering can adversely affect economies by making interest and exchange rates more volatile changing the demand for cash and by causing inflation in economies where criminals are engaged in business. The siphoning away of huge volumes of money from normal economic growth poses a real danger to the economies and affects the stability of the national and global market, it empowers and encourages corruption and organized crime. The money laundering offences are quite different and distinct from the general offences.  37. Furthermore, it stems out from the record that the accused-petitioner earlier submitted Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 22653 of 2018 for bail before this Court but the same was discharged for non-prosecution at the behest of the accused-petitioner. We are of the view that since earlier Rule was discharged for non prosecution on 1-8-2018 the accused-petitioner has come before this Court for bail within a very short intervals from the date of discharge of the Rule. Apart from this, as per section 20(Ka) Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the stipulated time frame for submitting investigating report within 180 days has not elapsed. 

 38. As far as the bail of FIR named accused No. 6 is concerned, the case of the present accused-petitioner is quite different and distinguishable from the case of co-accused. 

 39. Having considered the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, and the gravity of offences as alleged in the FIR we are led to hold that the accused-petitioner should not be enlarged on bail at this stage.
